items.headline: Bhutan certified free of dog-transmitted rabies
items.summary: The World Health Organization has validated that Bhutan has eliminated human deaths from dog-spread rabies, with zero cases recorded since June twenty twenty-three. The milestone followed years of nationwide dog vaccination campaigns run with local volunteers and community health workers.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a disease that still kills tens of thousands of people a year worldwide can be wiped out through sustained vaccination, even in a country with modest resources.

items.headline: FDA approves the first-ever drug for Alexander disease
items.summary: Regulators approved zilganersen, sold as Zanvastro, as the first treatment for Alexander disease, a rare and often fatal brain disorder in children. In the pivotal trial, patients on the drug kept a stable walking speed while those on placebo declined by about a third.
items.why_it_matters: Alexander disease has never had an approved treatment, so this is the first therapy that directly targets the underlying cause rather than just easing symptoms.
